t: 2026 in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
e: UDPS senior member Marie-Celestin Karondwa is beaten by residents of his neighbourhood in Butembo, North Kivu, after appearing on a radio programme promoting Ebola prevention measures.
Seventeen people are killed after a Let L-410 plane crashes into a residential area in Kenge, Kwango.
Security forces open fire to quell rioting at a cemetery in Beni, North Kivu, killing one person and injuring several others.
At least 41 people die when a boat carrying 100 passengers with cargo capsizes along Lake Tanganyika in Mapera.
At least 24 people are killed in a fire that destroys 300 houses and two schools in the Kadutu commmune of Bukavu.
Twenty-two people are killed in a wedding party fire in Kinshasa.
The Israeli and Congolese foreign ministries jointly state that the DRC will move its embassy from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem.
At least 13 civilians are killed by ADF militants in Banana École, outside Mambasa.

The US government announces that American citizens in the DRC will be temporarily barred from boarding commercial flights home and requires them to spend 21 days in a third country before traveling because of the 2026 Ebola epidemic.
A boat carrying students sinks at the confluence of the Sankuru and Kasai Rivers in Ilebo Territory, Kasaï Province, killing at least 20 people.

The Interior Minister issues an order banning public gatherings in Kinshasa, Tshopo, Haut-Uele, and Bas-Uele provinces, citing the risk of Ebola transmission and requiring enhanced health surveillance.

The government files a case against Rwanda at the International Court of Justice, alleging that Rwanda had violated international law through its alleged military involvement and support for armed groups in eastern DR Congo, and seeking reparations and an order for Rwanda to cease the alleged violations.
The Senate unanimously adopts a bill to amend the constitution, that will allow a referendum enabling President Tshisekedi to seek a third term.
The DRC participates at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
The United States imposes sanctions on M23 intelligence chief John Imani Nzenze and FDLR commander Gustave Kubwayo, as a result of their involvement in the ongoing DRC–Rwanda conflict.
Twenty people are killed in an ADF attack on a village in Beni Territory, North Kivu.
Authorities in Ituri Province ban funeral wakes and impose restrictions on gatherings, transport of bodies, and sporting events in an attempt to contain the spread of the 2026 Ebola epidemic there.
The government suspends mining activities for three months in Mwenga and Shabunda territories, citing illicit mining operations and mining fraud.
The Rwampara General Hospital is partially set on fire by residents protesting against the handling of the bodies of deceased Ebola victims.
Rwanda closes the Goma-Gisenyi border crossing with the DRC amid the 2026 Ituri Province Ebola epidemic.

The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) confirms an outbreak of Bundibugyo ebolavirus in Ituri Province; 246 cases and 80 deaths are reported, mainly in the Bunia, Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones.
M23 rebels withdraw from Sange in South Kivu.
At least 69 people are killed following a CODECO attack in Ituri province.
At least 26 people are killed following ADF attacks on villages in Ituri and North Kivu provinces.
The United States imposes sanctions on former president Joseph Kabila over his support for rebels in the eastern DRC.
The General Inspectorate of Mines announces the creation of a paramilitary unit to protect the country's mines with the help of US and UAE funding.

Authorities announce the rescue of least 200 civilians held captive by the ADF following a joint operation conducted by Congolese troops and the Uganda People's Defence Force along the Epulu river in eastern DRC.

The government announces it will begin receiving third country nationals deported from the United States under a new bilateral agreement; facilities begin preparation near Kinshasa, with costs covered by the US.
At least 43 civilians are killed in an assault by the ADF in Mambasa, Ituri Province.
The national football team defeats Jamaica 1-0 in Guadalajara, Mexico, in the inter-confederation play-off final; qualifying for the FIFA World Cup for the first time since 1974.

Veron Mosengo-Omba resigns as general secretary of the Confederation of African Football, amid controversy following the disputed 2025 Africa Cup of Nations Final decision to strip Senegal of the title after an appeal by the Royal Moroccan Football Federation.

A court in Belgium orders former diplomat Étienne Davignon to stand trial on charges of participation in war crimes in connection with the 1961 killing of former Congolese prime minister Patrice Lumumba. Davignon is the only surviving individual among those accused by Lumumba’s family of involvement in the case.
Three people, including a French United Nations aid worker, are killed in drone strikes in Goma with the occupying M23 rebels blaming the Congolese government.
At least 200 people are killed in a collapse at the Rubaya mines.
A suspected M23 drone attack is carried out on Kisangani Airport.

The government and the United States agree to a $1.2 billion strategic health partnership for 2026–2031, including $900 million in U.S. assistance and $300 million in increased domestic health spending.
Authorities announce the discovery of 171 bodies from two mass graves in Uvira.
Willy Ngoma, the spokesperson of M23, is killed in an FARDC drone strike near the Rubaya mines in North Kivu, along with at least eight others.
The Kavimvira border crossing between the DRC and Burundi reopens following a two-month closure caused by M23 offensives.
The ADF kills 66 people in an attack on Irumu, North Kivu.
